name: ng_based_nh3_wtg
source: Lee et al. (2022) Green Chem. 24:4830, doi 10.1039/D2GC00843B, accepted manuscript p. 13 and Fig. 8 (OSTI 1960296)
applicability_note: Conventional NG-based NH3, well-to-plant-gate. Onsite 2.30, upstream (NG production, electricity) 0.30.

name: nh3_process_co2
source: Lee et al. (2022), manuscript p. 13 (process CO2 from aMDEA unit, captured in version 1)
applicability_note: Concentrated process CO2 stream; Lee capture it fully (rate implicit, not stated as a percentage).

name: nh3_combustion_co2
source: Lee et al. (2022), manuscript p. 13 (boiler flue-gas CO2 captured with Cansolv in version 2)
applicability_note: Dilute combustion CO2 stream.

name: capture_penalty_process
unit: kg CO2e per kg CO2 captured
source: Derived from Lee et al. (2022) p. 13: version 1 net 1.16 minus (2.60 - 1.49) = 0.05 kg CO2e/kg NH3 for capture, compression, transport electricity
applicability_note: Derived by AmCraX arithmetic from published totals.

name: capture_penalty_combustion
unit: kg CO2e per kg CO2 captured
source: Derived from Lee et al. (2022) p. 13: version 2 net 0.77 minus (2.60 - 1.49 - 0.45) = 0.11; minus 0.05 for the process stream
applicability_note: Derived by AmCraX arithmetic from published totals.

name: ng_per_nh3
source: Lee et al. (2022) energy table: 32.52 GJ NG (LHV)/t NH3; NG LHV 47.1 MJ/kg (manuscript p. 8)
applicability_note: Used to convert an upstream methane leakage rate into kg CH4 per kg NH3. Whole NG mass treated as CH4 (upper-bound simplification).

name: blue_nh3_lee_v1
source: Lee et al. (2022) p. 13 (carbon-capturing NH3 version 1)
applicability_note: Reproduced by blue_nh3_ef(capture_process=1).

name: blue_nh3_lee_v2
source: Lee et al. (2022) p. 13 (carbon-capturing NH3 version 2)
applicability_note: Reproduced by blue_nh3_ef(1, 1).

name: green_nh3_lee
source: Lee et al. (2022) p. 13 (renewable NH3 WTG = 0; equipment manufacture excluded)
applicability_note: Boundary limitation, not a claim that green NH3 is emission-free.

name: embedded_renewable_h2_low
source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2024, 'GHG emissions of hydrogen and its derivatives', highlights: embedded emissions of renewable assets 0.4-2.7 kg CO2-eq/kg H2
applicability_note: Converted to per kg NH3 with 0.1775 kg H2/kg NH3 (stoichiometry). Only the page highlights were read.

name: embedded_renewable_h2_high
source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2024 (as above)
applicability_note: Upper end of the embedded-emissions range.

name: grey_nh3_range_low
source: cechetto2023membrane p. 19 (2.0-4.6 t CO2/t NH3), as recorded in amcrax/data/environmental.yaml
applicability_note: Lower end of the quoted grey-ammonia range.

name: grey_nh3_range_high
source: cechetto2023membrane p. 19, as above
applicability_note: Upper end; likely includes coal-based plants.

name: coal_nh3_low
source: Zhang et al. (2022) Int. J. Life Cycle Assess. 27:50-61, doi 10.1007/s11367-021-02010-z ('Life cycle assessment of ammonia synthesis in China'; coal gasification routes): 3.88 -> 2.18 kg GHG per kg NH3
applicability_note: LOW CONFIDENCE: abstract-level value from a search extract; the publisher page could not be opened; boundary and unit not verified.

name: coal_nh3_high
source: as above (older gasification technology)
applicability_note: LOW CONFIDENCE, see coal_nh3_low.

name: gwp100_ch4_fossil
source: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch. 7 Table 7.15 (fossil CH4, GWP-100); US EPA 'Understanding Global Warming Potentials' confirms the AR6 range 27-30 (accessed 2026-11-23)
applicability_note: The exact 29.8 is from AR6 Table 7.15; the IPCC PDF returned HTTP 403 in this session so only the EPA range was re-checked.

name: gwp100_n2o
source: IPCC AR6 WGI Ch. 7 Table 7.15; US EPA page accessed 2026-11-23 states 273

name: ship_ef
source: GLEC Framework v3.0 liquefied-gas tanker 100-199 kcbm, VLSFO, WTW, via Climatiq listing (see amcrax/data/environmental.yaml)
applicability_note: Generic liquefied-gas carrier, not ammonia specific. Applied per tonne NH3 cargo, one way, no ballast return.

name: ship_distance_baseline_km
source: amcrax/data/environmental.yaml (existing illustrative assumption)
applicability_note: Route distance is a SCENARIO parameter. No sea-distance dataset could be opened in this session (port-distance site refused the connection), so Middle East and Australia distances are not quoted.

name: ship_distance_range_km
source: scenario bounds chosen by AmCraX to span regional to long-haul voyages
applicability_note: Sensitivity bounds only; the shipping term is small either way (0.011 x 12000 / 1000 = 0.13 kg CO2e/kg NH3).

name: boil_off_fraction
source: no sourced boil-off or terminal-loss value found; excluded by default
applicability_note: Parameter kept in the model (default 0). Not varied because no source supports a value.

name: grid_ef_singapore_2024
source: EMA, Singapore Energy Statistics Ch. 2: average Grid Emission Factor 0.412 (2023) -> 0.402 (2024); page text confirmed by search extract 2026-11-23, https://www.ema.gov.sg/singapore-energy-statistics/Ch02/index2
applicability_note: Operating-margin average. Used both for process electricity and as the 'average grid' comparator.

name: ng_co2_ef
source: IPCC 2006 Guidelines Vol. 2 Ch. 2 Table 2.2 (natural gas)
applicability_note: Combustion CO2 only.

name: ng_lhv
source: Lee et al. (2022) manuscript p. 8 (NG LHV 47.1 MJ/kg)
applicability_note: Used to convert NG leakage fraction to kg CH4 per MWh.

name: ccgt_efficiency
source: no Singapore plant-level source retrieved; range 0.50-0.60
applicability_note: Net electrical efficiency (LHV) of the natural-gas CCGT comparator. Compare the EMA grid average above, which is a mix of plants.

name: ccgt_efficiency_range
source: scenario bounds
applicability_note: Sensitivity bounds.

name: ng_upstream_leak_scenarios
source: Leakage cases 0.2 %, 1.5 %, 3.0 % named in Analysis of Hydrogen Production Costs across the United States (arXiv 2206.10689), seen in a search extract only; Agora Energiewende chart cites 0.15 % (Norway) and 1.2 % (Russia) cases
applicability_note: LOW CONFIDENCE for the exact values (full text not opened). Used as scenario values for methane leakage; default is 0 (lower bound).

name: smr_h2_unabated
source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2024, GHG emissions chapter highlights: unabated natural gas 10-12 kg CO2-eq/kg H2; 75-95 % occurs at the production site
applicability_note: Central value taken as the midpoint 11.

name: smr_h2_ccs
source: Elgowainy et al. (2024) Front. Energy Res. 12:1473383, doi 10.3389/fenrg.2024.1473383 (introduction, summary of other studies: SMR with CCS 3.4-3.6 kg CO2e/kg H2), search extract only
applicability_note: LOW CONFIDENCE: capture rate and boundary not confirmed. Upper sensitivity 5.3 (90 % CCS, 3 % methane leakage, arXiv 2206.10689 interpolation).

name: smr_h2_ccs_high
source: arXiv 2206.10689 (search extract): 5.3 with 90 % CCS at 3.0 % leakage; 12.9 without CCS
applicability_note: LOW CONFIDENCE, upper sensitivity only.

name: ahmad_gas_flow_per_MWh
source: Ahmad et al. (2025) IJHE 173:151337 Table 6 (Case 2a: gas flow 150.52 t/h, W_net 43.1 MW)
applicability_note: Used only to turn exhaust ppmv values into mass per MWh. Assumes the ppmv values refer to the whole turbine exhaust stream (not stated unambiguously).

name: ahmad_n2o_ppmv_vnh3
source: Ahmad et al. (2025) p. 9 (Chemkin simulation, VNH3 case)
applicability_note: SIMULATED, not measured. Experiments cited by the paper show higher NO (282-337 ppmv).

name: ahmad_no_ppmv_vnh3
source: Ahmad et al. (2025) p. 9 (Chemkin simulation, VNH3 case)
applicability_note: SIMULATED; Chemkin underestimates NO per the paper. Local pollutant: reported separately.

name: flue_gas_molar_mass
source: air-like exhaust approximation
applicability_note: Used to convert ppmv to mass fraction.

name: carbon_tax_sg_2026
source: NEA Singapore carbon tax page (accessed 2026-11-23): SGD 25 in 2024-25, SGD 45 in 2026-27, SGD 50-80 by 2030; facilities emitting >= 25,000 t CO2e/yr direct; covers CO2, CH4, N2O
applicability_note: Applies only to direct in-scope Singapore emissions. Reported in SGD; no exchange rate is sourced, so it is not added to USD costs.

name: eta_direct_ahmad
source: Ahmad 2025 Table 6 Case 2a (LHV 18.8 MJ/kg basis)
applicability_note: Literature-calibrated scenario input, not an Aspen result.

name: eta_full_crack_ahmad
source: Ahmad 2025 p. 15 (alpha = 0, about 54 %)
applicability_note: Exhaust-heated cracker, PR 8; value read from text, approximate.

name: eta_gt_gas
source: electricity per kg NH3 of Ahmad Case 2a re-expressed on the AmCraX LHV basis (18.6 MJ/kg)
applicability_note: Applied to every gaseous fuel in the fired and purified variants.
